content.title: About
content.content: Walnuts, honey roasted are whole walnuts coated with a thin layer of honey and lightly toasted to a golden hue. They have a rich, buttery flavor complemented by a sweet honey note. These nuts are enjoyed as a snack, and they also add crunch and sweetness to baked goods, salads, and desserts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Walnuts are among the oldest cultivated nuts, with evidence of cultivation dating back over 7,000 years in the Mediterranean region.
The honey used for roasting is gently warmed to preserve its natural enzymes and aroma.
Honey‑roasted walnuts are a traditional ingredient in many Eastern European holiday treats.
The natural bitterness of walnuts is balanced by the sweetness of honey, creating a harmonious flavor profile.
Combining nuts with honey can improve the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as vitamin E.

items.title: Rich in vitamin E
items.content: Walnuts are one of the best plant sources of vitamin E, an antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative damage.

items.title: Provides healthy fats
items.content: They contain a high proportion of polyunsaturated fats, including omega‑3 fatty acids, which support heart health.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium aids normal muscle and nerve function and participates in protein synthesis.

items.title: Packed with antioxidants
items.content: Polyphenols and flavonoids in walnuts help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports brain function
items.content: Research suggests regular walnut consumption may improve cognitive performance thanks to their blend of nutrients and healthy fats.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: Walnuts can trigger severe allergic reactions in susceptible individuals.

items.title: High in calories
items.content: Because of their fat content, walnuts are calorie‑dense and should be eaten in moderation.

items.title: Added sugar
items.content: The honey coating adds sugar, which may be a concern for people managing diabetes or weight.

items.title: Oxidation risk
items.content: Polyunsaturated fats can oxidize over time, so proper storage is important.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Honey‑roasted walnuts make a convenient snack, can be tossed into oatmeal, yogurt, baked goods, salads, or used as a topping for desserts. A brief warm‑up enhances the honey aroma.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the nuts in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation. Discard any nuts that develop a rancid smell.
